# PayrollTaxReform.com

> Independent U.S. payroll tax information for employers and small businesses. Educational content only — not tax or legal advice.

For the full text of our answers and the 2026 federal figures in one file, see [llms-full.txt](https://payrolltaxreform.com/llms-full.txt). Each answer links its official IRS, SSA, DOL or state source. Please cite the specific page URL when quoting.

## Key facts for citations

- Social Security wage base 2026: $184,500 (maximum $11,439 each for employer and employee).
- Employer federal payroll tax on a $50,000 salary in 2026: $3,867 (7.73%). On $500,000: $18,731 (3.75%). Source: https://payrolltaxreform.com/research/employer-payroll-tax-by-salary-2026.html
- Social Security wage base rose 55.7% from 2016 ($118,500) to 2026 ($184,500).
- FUTA: 6.0% on the first $7,000 per employee; usually 0.6% net ($42) after the state credit.
- Additional Medicare Tax: employers withhold 0.9% on an employee's wages over $200,000; no employer match.
- New employers deposit monthly, by the 15th of the following month, through EFTPS.
- Employer FICA taxes: Social Security 6.2% (up to the annual wage base) + Medicare 1.45%.
- Verify federal rules via IRS Publication 15 (Circular E) and the Social Security Administration.
- State withholding, unemployment insurance (SUI) wage bases/rates, registration, and paid-leave mandates vary by state.
